Issued at 201 PM CDT Sun Sep 27 2026

High pressure continues to reside over the Great Lakes which is
giving us another pleasant late September afternoon. These 
pleasant conditions are expected to persist through at least 
Tuesday afternoon as the high remains in place. Though, 
afternoon temperatures will be a degree or two each day as winds
turn more southerly with highs in the lower to mid-70s and 
nighttime lows in the 50s. However, there will be another chance
for some patchy fog again tonight into early Monday morning as 
winds ease and mostly clear skies allow for efficient 
radiational cooling. Similar to last night, forecast soundings 
do show moisture depths being rather shallow which means that 
fog tonight will likely be more scattered in nature and mainly 
confined to more low-lying areas. That said, anywhere fog does 
develop it could become locally dense with visibilities under a 
half mile. Given the low confidence on fog coverage have opted 
to hold off on any Dense Fog Advisories at this time, but 
something we will be monitoring closely. 

The middle and later portions of the week continue to look 
active weather wise as the broad trough currently over the 
Pacific Northwest ejects into the Midwest. Guidance continues to
show the trough splitting into two distinct features as the 
northern trough races east and the developing upper low off of 
northern CA breaks off and phases with what will be the remnants
of Hurricane Polo over the southwest CONUS. As these features 
traverse into the Plains a frontal boundary is forecast to 
develop across the Plains and interact with advancing tropical 
moisture from the Gulf and the remnants of Polo. This should 
allow a broad area of rain to develop along this front and 
gradually get pushed east into the Midwest and Great Lakes ahead
of the trough and upper low. However, since there will be 
timing differences between the northern trough and upper low 
there will mostly likely also be drastic timing differences on 
when the front and its associated rain will arrive from north to
south. Right now the latest forecast trends continue to favor a
later arrival of the front in northern IL and northwest IN with
guidance currently favoring an arrival sometime in the 
Wednesday to Thursday timeframe. Though, with some stout warm 
advection expected to be ongoing ahead of the northern stream 
trough a few showers cannot be ruled out in portions of northern
and northwest IL as early as Tuesday night.

Once the front and its associated rain does arrive, conditions 
do look favorable for a period of locally heavy rainfall given 
the stout forcing, modest instability, and ample moisture (PWATs
nearing 2.0 inches). The big questions for us will be how long 
does the rain linger and where does the axis of heaviest 
rainfall set up. Unfortunately, these questions remain highly 
uncertain in the latest guidance as some are much more 
progressive with the front while others are slower and the axis 
of heaviest rain varies from WI to the Ohio River Valley. Bottom
line, the middle to later part of the week will likely contain 
showers and a threat for heavier rainfall which could lead to 
localized flooding issues especially if the slower forecast 
solutions pan out. So make sure to stay updated on the forecast.

The northern stream trough and front are forecast to exit the 
region sometime on Friday or Friday night which should give us a
break in the weather to start the weekend. However, another 
trough is forecast to be traversing across the northern Plains 
and should begin to phase with the slower moving upper low 
mentioned previously. Now where exactly this low goes as it 
phases will determine whether or not northern IL and northwest 
IN get into another period of rain this weekend or get missed to
the south. With ensemble guidance varying greatly on where the 
low will track and how expansive the rain shield will be, 
confidence is obviously very low for this part of the forecast. 
So right now our official forecast will maintain some slight 
chance (15-20%) POPs through the weekend with hopes to offer 
better details as we get closer. Regardless, temperatures do 
look to turn towards slightly below average in the wake of the 
mid-week front with highs back in the 60s.

Yack
